lessons.title: Hundreds, tens and ones
lessons.art_alt: The castle guard waits by stacks of hundred, ten and one blocks

hook.text: The Place Value Castle gate opens with a magic number. Tonight the guard needs 243 blocks. Carrying 243 single blocks would take all night! Can you use the big blocks?
hook.say: The Place Value Castle gate opens with a magic number. Tonight the guard needs 243 blocks. Carrying 243 single blocks would take all night! Can you use the big blocks?

discover.text: Build the number with castle blocks. Drag a block onto the mat or tap it. Tap ➖ to take one back.
discover.hint: Start with the biggest blocks. How many hundreds? Then tens, then ones.
discover.say: Build the number with castle blocks. Drag a block onto the mat or tap it. Tap ➖ to take one back.

rule.text: In 243, the 2 means 2 hundreds, the 4 means 4 tens and the 3 means 3 ones. 200 + 40 + 3 = 243. A zero means none: 306 has no tens.
examples: Each place holds 0 to 9. Ten ones make a ten; ten tens make a hundred.
rule.say: In 243, the 2 means 2 hundreds, the 4 means 4 tens and the 3 means 3 ones. 200 plus 40 plus 3 equals 243. A zero means none: 306 has no tens.
sayEx: 243 equals 2 hundreds plus 4 tens plus 3 ones
306 equals 3 hundreds plus 0 tens plus 6 ones
Each place holds 0 to 9. Ten ones make a ten; ten tens make a hundred.

check.q: What is the digit 5 worth in 352?

notes.5: 5 is the digit, but it sits in the tens place, so it is worth 5 tens = 50.
notes.500: 500 would be 5 hundreds. In 352 the hundreds digit is 3.

check.explain: 352 = 3 hundreds, 5 tens, 2 ones. The 5 is worth 5 tens = 50.
check.say: What is the digit 5 worth in 352?

notes.470: 470 has 7 tens and 0 ones. We need 0 tens and 7 ones: 407.
notes.47: 47 has no hundreds. We need 4 hundreds: 407.

check.explain: Write a 0 for the empty tens place: 4 0 7 = 407.

notes.6209: Don't write 600, 20 and 9 side by side! 6 hundreds, 2 tens, 9 ones = 629.
notes.692: 692 swaps the tens and ones: it has 9 tens and 2 ones.

reteach.text: Here's another way. Think of money! A \$100 note, \$10 notes and \$1 coins. \$243 is two \$100 notes, four \$10 notes and three \$1 coins. The digits tell you how many of each.

discover.text: Build 125 with the blocks, like one \$100 note, two \$10 notes and five \$1 coins.
discover.say: Build 125 with the blocks, like one 100 dollar note, two 10 dollar notes and five 1 dollar coins.

reteach.say: Here's another way. Think of money! A 100 dollar note, 10 dollar notes and 1 dollar coins. 243 dollars is two 100 dollar notes, four 10 dollar notes and three 1 dollar coins. The digits tell you how many of each.

check2.q: In 718, what is the digit 1 worth?

notes.1: The 1 sits in the tens place, so it is worth 1 ten = 10.
notes.100: 100 would be the hundreds place. In 718 the hundreds digit is 7.

check2.explain: 718 = 7 hundreds, 1 ten, 8 ones. The 1 is worth 10.
check2.say: In 718, what is the digit 1 worth?

notes.250: 250 has 5 tens. We need 0 tens and 5 ones: 205.
notes.25: 25 has no hundreds. We need 2 hundreds: 205.

check2.explain: No tens, so write 0 in the tens place: 205.

notes.3408: Don't write the parts side by side. 3 hundreds, 4 tens, 8 ones = 348.

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Whole Numbers: numbers to 1000, place value (hundreds, tens, ones), number notation and expanded form.

lessons.title: Adding with regrouping
lessons.art_alt: The candy fairy beside a full gumdrop jar and bags of ten

hook.text: Gumdrop the candy fairy has 28 gumdrops and gets 15 more. Her ones jar can only hold 9 loose gumdrops. What happens when it gets too full?
hook.say: Gumdrop the candy fairy has 28 gumdrops and gets 15 more. Her ones jar can only hold 9 loose gumdrops. What happens when it gets too full?

discover.text: Move the new gumdrops into the ones jar. Drag them or tap them. When the jar has 10, bundle them into a ten-bag!
discover.hint: 10 loose gumdrops can become 1 ten-bag. Tap 🎀 Bundle when the jar has 10.
discover.say: Move the new gumdrops into the ones jar. Drag them or tap them. When the jar has 10, bundle them into a ten-bag!

rule.text: Add the ones first: 8 + 5 = 13 ones. Ten ones make 1 ten, so write 3 and carry 1 ten. Then add the tens: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4 tens. So 28 + 15 = 43.
rule.say: Add the ones first: 8 plus 5 equals 13 ones. Ten ones make 1 ten, so write 3 and carry 1 ten. Then add the tens: 2 plus 1 plus 1 equals 4 tens. So 28 plus 15 equals 43.
sayEx: 28 plus 15 equals 43 (8 plus 5 equals 13: write 3, carry 1)

notes.33: 6 + 7 = 13 ones. Carry the 1 ten: 3 tens + 1 ten = 4 tens, so 43.
notes.313: 13 ones is 1 ten and 3 ones. Carry the ten instead of writing 13: 43.

check.q: In 47 + 25, the ones make 7 + 5 = 12. What do we write in the ones place?

notes.12: Only one digit fits in the ones place. 12 = 1 ten and 2 ones: write 2, carry 1.
notes.1: The 1 is the ten we carry to the tens. The ones digit is 2.

check.say: In 47 plus 25, the ones make 7 plus 5 equals 12. What do we write in the ones place?

notes.182: 4 + 8 = 12: write 2 and carry 1 ten. 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 tens. So 192.
notes.1812: Don't write 12 in the ones place; carry the 1 ten: 192.

reteach.text: Here's another way: make a friendly ten! 28 is close to 30. Take 2 gumdrops from the 15 to make 30. Now 13 are left. 30 + 13 = 43. Same answer!

discover.text: Fill the jar to make a friendly ten, then bundle it!
discover.hint: The jar has 9. One more makes 10, then bundle!
discover.say: Fill the jar to make a friendly ten, then bundle it!

reteach.say: Here's another way: make a friendly ten! 28 is close to 30. Take 2 gumdrops from the 15 to make 30. Now 13 are left. 30 plus 13 equals 43. Same answer!

notes.13: 8 + 5 = 13 ones. Carry the 1 ten: 1 + 1 = 2 tens, so 23.
notes.113: 13 ones = 1 ten and 3 ones. Carry the ten: 23.

notes.313: Carry the ten instead of writing 13: 43.

check2.q: In 65 + 28, how many tens are there after carrying?

notes.8: 6 + 2 = 8 tens, plus the 1 ten carried from 5 + 8 = 13: 9 tens.

check2.say: In 65 plus 28, how many tens are there after carrying?

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Addition within 1000 with regrouping (carrying), with the 'make ten' mental strategy.

lessons.title: Times means equal groups
lessons.art_alt: Fairies dance around three mushroom fairy rings

hook.text: Tonight is the fairy dance! Every fairy ring needs the same number of mushrooms, or the magic won't work. Can you build the rings?
hook.say: Tonight is the fairy dance! Every fairy ring needs the same number of mushrooms, or the magic won't work. Can you build the rings?

discover.text: Make 3 fairy rings with 4 mushrooms in each. Drag a mushroom into a ring, or tap a ring to add one.
discover.hint: Every ring gets the same: 4 mushrooms each.
discover.say: Make 3 fairy rings with 4 mushrooms in each. Drag a mushroom into a ring, or tap a ring to add one.

rule.text: 3 groups of 4 is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. We write it 3 × 4 = 12. The first number tells how many groups; the second tells how many in each group.
rule.say: 3 groups of 4 is 4 plus 4 plus 4 equals 12. We write it 3 times 4 equals 12. The first number tells how many groups; the second tells how many in each group.

notes.5 + 2 = 7: That adds one 5 and one 2. 5 groups of 2 is 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10.

notes.5 bags with 5 sweets in each: That is 5 groups of 5 = 5 × 5. We need 3 groups.
notes.3 bags with 3 sweets in each: That is 3 × 3. We need 5 in each group.

check.q: 4 fairy rings have 10 mushrooms each. How many mushrooms?
check.say: 4 fairy rings have 10 mushrooms each. How many mushrooms?

reteach.text: Here's another way: skip-count! Hop along a number line in jumps of the same size. 3 jumps of 4: 4… 8… 12! The number of jumps is the number of groups.

discover.text: Build 2 rings of 5 and count in 5s!
discover.say: Build 2 rings of 5 and count in 5s!

reteach.say: Here's another way: skip-count! Hop along a number line in jumps of the same size. 3 jumps of 4: 4… 8… 12! The number of jumps is the number of groups.

notes.2 + 3 = 5: That adds 2 and 3. 2 groups of 3 is 3 + 3 = 6.

notes.4 groups of 4: That is 4 × 4. We need 2 in each group.

check2.q: 3 plates have 5 cakes each. How many cakes?
check2.say: 3 plates have 5 cakes each. How many cakes?

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Multiplication: the concept of multiplication as equal groups (number of groups × number in each group), multiplication tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10.

lessons.title: Sharing fairly
lessons.art_alt: Crumb the baker dragon brings cookies to four bear cubs

hook.text: Crumb the little baker dragon baked 12 cookies for four bear cubs. If one cub gets more than the others, there will be grumbles! Can you share them fairly?
hook.say: Crumb the little baker dragon baked 12 cookies for four bear cubs. If one cub gets more than the others, there will be grumbles! Can you share them fairly?

discover.text: Share the cookies so every plate gets the same. Drag a cookie to a plate, tap a plate, or tap Deal one each.
discover.hint: Give one cookie to each plate, then go round again until they're all gone.
discover.say: Share the cookies so every plate gets the same. Drag a cookie to a plate, tap a plate, or tap Deal one each.

rule.text: Sharing equally is dividing. 12 cookies shared among 4 plates is 3 each. We write 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Check with times: 4 × 3 = 12.
rule.say: Sharing equally is dividing. 12 cookies shared among 4 plates is 3 each. We write 12 divided by 4 equals 3. Check with times: 4 times 3 equals 12.

check.q: 12 stickers are shared equally between 2 children. How many does each child get?

notes.10: That's 12 − 2. Sharing means splitting into 2 equal groups: 6 and 6.
notes.14: Sharing makes each share smaller, not bigger. 12 ÷ 2 = 6.

check.say: 12 stickers are shared equally between 2 children. How many does each child get?

notes.5: 5 is the number of groups. Each group gets 4, because 5 × 4 = 20.
notes.15: That is 20 − 5. Sharing 20 into 5 equal groups gives 4.

check.q: 10 cupcakes are put on plates, 2 on each plate. How many plates are needed?

notes.2: 2 is how many go on each plate. Count the groups of 2 in 10: 5 plates.

check.say: 10 cupcakes are put on plates, 2 on each plate. How many plates are needed?

reteach.text: Here's another way: use times tables backwards! 12 ÷ 4 asks: 4 times what makes 12? 4 × 3 = 12, so each cub gets 3.

discover.text: Share 8 cookies between 2 plates. Then think: 2 times what makes 8?
discover.hint: Deal one each until they're gone.
discover.say: Share 8 cookies between 2 plates. Then think: 2 times what makes 8?

reteach.say: Here's another way: use times tables backwards! 12 divided by 4 asks: 4 times what makes 12? 4 times 3 equals 12, so each cub gets 3.

check2.q: 8 apples are shared equally among 4 friends. How many does each friend get?

notes.4: 4 is the number of friends. 4 × 2 = 8, so each gets 2.

check2.say: 8 apples are shared equally among 4 friends. How many does each friend get?

notes.10: 10 is the number of groups. 10 × 3 = 30, so each gets 3.

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Division: sharing equally and grouping, division as the inverse of multiplication (tables 2, 3, 4, 5, 10).

lessons.title: Halves, thirds and quarters
lessons.art_alt: The star fairy cuts a party pizza for her friends

hook.text: The star fairy is cutting a party pizza for her friends. If the slices aren't the same size, someone gets a tiny piece! How do we cut it fairly?
hook.say: The star fairy is cutting a party pizza for her friends. If the slices aren't the same size, someone gets a tiny piece! How do we cut it fairly?

discover.text: Slide to cut the pizza into equal slices, then tap the slices to colour them.
discover.hint: Quarters means 4 equal parts. Thirds means 3 equal parts.

stages.text: Cut the pizza into quarters (4 equal slices), then colour 1 slice.
stages.say: Cut the pizza into quarters (4 equal slices), then colour 1 slice.

stages.text: Now cut the chocolate bar into thirds (3 equal parts) and colour 2 parts.
stages.say: Now cut the chocolate bar into thirds (3 equal parts) and colour 2 parts.

discover.say: Slide to cut the pizza into equal slices, then tap the slices to colour them.

rule.text: 2 equal parts are halves, 3 equal parts are thirds, and 4 equal parts are quarters. In $\frac{1}{4}$, the bottom number tells how many equal parts there are; the top number tells how many we take.
rule.say: 2 equal parts are halves, 3 equal parts are thirds, and 4 equal parts are quarters. In the fraction one over four, the bottom number, four, tells how many equal parts there are. The top number, one, tells how many we take.
sayEx: one quarter equals one quarter , two thirds equals two thirds

check.q: A cake is cut into 4 equal pieces. One piece is…

notes.one half ($\\frac{1}{2}$): A half is one of 2 equal parts. This cake has 4 equal parts: a quarter.
notes.one third ($\\frac{1}{3}$): A third is one of 3 equal parts. This cake has 4: a quarter.

check.explain: 4 equal parts → each is one quarter, $\frac{1}{4}$.
check.say: A cake is cut into 4 equal pieces. One piece is…

options: a sandwich cut into 2 equal parts
a sandwich cut into 2 parts, one big and one small
a sandwich cut into 3 equal parts

notes.a sandwich cut into 2 parts, one big and: Halves must be EQUAL. A big part and a small part are not halves.
notes.a sandwich cut into 3 equal parts: 3 equal parts are thirds, not halves.

check.q: A bar has 3 equal parts and 2 parts are coloured. What fraction is coloured?

notes.$\\frac{1}{3}$: $\frac{1}{3}$ is one part. Two parts are coloured: $\frac{2}{3}$.
notes.$\\frac{3}{2}$: The bottom number is how many equal parts in all (3). The top is how many are coloured (2): $\frac{2}{3}$.

check.say: A bar has 3 equal parts and 2 parts are coloured. What fraction is coloured?

reteach.text: Here's another way: fold paper! Fold a strip in half once and you get 2 equal parts. Fold it in half again and you get 4 equal parts. The more equal parts, the smaller each part is.

discover.text: Fold the paper strip in half, then colour one half.

stages.text: Cut the strip into halves (2 equal parts) and colour 1 part.
stages.say: Cut the strip into halves (2 equal parts) and colour 1 part.

discover.say: Fold the paper strip in half, then colour one half.

reteach.say: Here's another way: fold paper! Fold a strip in half once and you get 2 equal parts. Fold it in half again and you get 4 equal parts. The more equal parts, the smaller each part is.

check2.q: A pizza is cut into 3 equal slices. One slice is…

notes.one quarter ($\\frac{1}{4}$): A quarter is one of 4 equal parts. This pizza has 3: a third.
notes.one half ($\\frac{1}{2}$): A half is one of 2 equal parts. This pizza has 3: a third.

check2.explain: 3 equal parts → each is one third, $\frac{1}{3}$.
check2.say: A pizza is cut into 3 equal slices. One slice is…

check2.q: Which is bigger: $\frac{1}{2}$ or $\frac{1}{4}$ of the same pizza?

notes.$\\frac{1}{4}$: Cutting into 4 makes smaller slices than cutting into 2. A half is bigger.
notes.they are the same: Fold once for halves, twice for quarters: quarters are smaller. $\frac{1}{2}$ is bigger.

check2.explain: Fewer equal parts → bigger parts. $\frac{1}{2}$ is bigger than $\frac{1}{4}$.
check2.say: Which is bigger: one half or one quarter of the same pizza?

check2.q: A bar has 4 equal parts and 3 are coloured. What fraction is coloured?

notes.$\\frac{1}{4}$: $\frac{1}{4}$ is one part. Three parts are coloured: $\frac{3}{4}$.
notes.$\\frac{4}{3}$: The bottom number is the parts in all (4), the top is the coloured parts (3): $\frac{3}{4}$.

check2.say: A bar has 4 equal parts and 3 are coloured. What fraction is coloured?

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Fractions: fraction of a whole (halves, thirds, quarters), equal parts, notation, comparing unit fractions.
